title: Meat Balls (Deep-Fried, Ketchup-Glazed)
description: Meat Balls (Deep-Fried, Ketchup-Glazed) are crisp, golden meatballs with a tender, juicy center, finished in a warm tomato ketchup glaze. This classic continental-style appetizer is ideal for buffets, cocktail parties, or as a hearty main course served with mashed potatoes and seasonal vegetables.

ingredients.title: Ingredients
items: Minced meat – 500 grams (beef or beef-pork mix recommended)

ingredients.title: For Frying
items: Neutral oil (sunflower or canola) – as needed for deep frying

instruction.title: 1. Prepare the Meatball Mix
steps: In a mixing bowl, combine the minced meat, chopped onion, parsley, salt, pepper, nutmeg, egg, and breadcrumbs.
Mix gently by hand until just combined. Do not overwork the mixture.
Optional: Rest the mixture in the refrigerator for 15–20 minutes for easier shaping and better binding.

instruction.title: 2. Shape
steps: Portion the mixture into even balls (25–30g each). Lightly moisten hands with water or oil to prevent sticking.
Optional: Roll each meatball in extra breadcrumbs for a crispier crust.

instruction.title: 3. Frying
steps: Heat oil in a deep fryer or heavy-bottomed pan to 170–180°C (340–355°F).
Fry meatballs in small batches for 3–5 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and fully cooked.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels or a wire rack.

instruction.title: 4. Glazing
steps: Warm the tomato ketchup in a small pan over low heat.
Once meatballs are fried, toss them in the warm ketchup or brush lightly to glaze just before serving.

instruction.title: 5. Serving Suggestions
steps: Serve hot as an appetizer with cocktail picks.
Pair with creamy mashed potatoes or buttered vegetables for a plated main course.
Ideal for buffets or hors d’oeuvres service with a small herb garnish (e.g. parsley or chive).

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve hot as an appetizer with cocktail picks.
Pair with creamy mashed potatoes or buttered vegetables for a plated main course.
Ideal for buffets or hors d’oeuvres service with a small herb garnish such as parsley or chive.

chefTips: Lightly sautéing the onion before mixing adds sweetness and improves flavor.
For extra tenderness, soak breadcrumbs in 30 ml milk before mixing.
To elevate the glaze, mix ketchup with a dash of Worcestershire sauce, honey, or Dijon mustard.
Fry in small batches to maintain the oil temperature and ensure even browning.
